what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat a condition called transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). This is a heart disease where a protein called transthyretin misfolds and builds up in the heart muscle, making it stiff and weak. Tafamidis works by stabilizing this protein to slow down the damage to your heart.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not crush, cut, chew, or open the capsule. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you have trouble swallowing the capsule, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before changing how you take it.
dosing: The usual dose is: Vyndamax (tafamidis) — one 61 mg capsule taken by mouth once daily. Vyndaqel (tafamidis meglumine) — four 20 mg capsules taken by mouth once daily (total of 80 mg). Your doctor will decide which form and dose is right for you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use if the expiration date on the package has passed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines that may interact with tafamidis without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, especially medicines that affect a protein called OATP1B1/1B3 (such as certain cholesterol-lowering drugs). Avoid making changes to your diet or starting new supplements without talking to your healthcare team. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: worsening shortness of breath, unusual swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet, sudden weight gain (more than 2–3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week), chest pain or pressure, feeling faint or dizzy, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or any new or unusual symptoms. Also call your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine may not be safe for your baby.
when_it_works: Tafamidis works continuously to stabilize the transthyretin protein and slow the progression of heart disease. You may not feel an immediate difference, but the medicine is working to help protect your heart over time. Most patients notice benefits over months to years. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine may harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for one month after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Older adults: No dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your doctor may need to monitor you more carefully. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
